source_en: Home to the harbor flats after cards.
Cards until dawn. Going home to sleep.
Settling a sports debt with a friend.
Basement game by the tram depot. Home now.
Checking on my hidden "nest egg."
Metropol's shut. Home to count what's left.
Folded early. Back to my lockdown bunk.
Going home to fold my hand.
Resident check-in. The odds say show up.
State Savings Bank teller. Home by six.
Visiting for the week. I live in Batumi.
Handing in my pension papers.
Off to the Metropol card room. Open nightly.
Off duty from the militia post.
Moving in with an uncle. New to the city.
Monastery novice, returning for prayers.
Sixty-five and retired. Collecting my veteran's card.
Arriving from Poti to register as resident.
Heads or tails, officer? Kidding. Here are my documents.
I'm betting on the city's quick recovery. The spread looks good.
I put everything on the "red sky" theory. I'm cleaning up.
The house always wins. Right now, the house is falling down.
One last spin. Let's see if my ID still carries value.
Luck is a lady, but she left on the last bus.
My lucky streak continues! See you next turn.
Thanks. Five-to-one you're still here tomorrow.
Stakes are too high for me now. Take care.
Corner pocket. Fine. I've bluffed out of worse hands.
Two-to-one I'm out by morning. I like those odds.
Funny… three aces… and still not enough…
House always wins… should have… bet on that…
Where are you coming from?
The Metropol back room. Cards till dawn. Now home to sleep it off.
The Metropol shut at curfew. Now it's a basement game by the tram depot.
A cellar across the river. Three players, one candle. I folded early.
The evening train from Kutaisi. First time in your town, officer.
Loading freighters at the port. Honest work. I quit cards years ago.
The Metropol. The card room's open again. Full tables all night!
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Sweaty palms, as always. Bad for holding cards, good for bluffing.
I sleep all afternoon and wake tired. The numbers won't sit still.
I forget whole hands now. Twenty years, I never forgot a card.
Nothing. Dry hands, steady as a surgeon. Always have been.
No late nights since I quit cards. I sleep like a Party official.
Nothing. At forty-five a man paces himself. Rest, eat, no trouble.
You have a poker face that would bankrupt me in ten minutes.
The odds keep shifting. I keep adjusting. That's all you can do.
I found a four-leaf clover in the ash. Taking that as a sign.
The house always wins, does it not? Right now it's on fire.
No out-bluffing the end of the world. Going home to fold.
Every player knows when to walk away. I'm almost there.
